work: P01 Gazi, Prappo, Hossain 2026, 'Cross-Network NetFlow Intrusion Detection: A Controlled Benchmark of Transfer, Adaptation and Target Reference Windows' (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.24172400 -> record 24172401, code v1.0.0)
source_opened: Zenodo metadata + full code archive (README, docs/PROTOCOL.md, docs/EXPERIMENTS.md, crossnet/methods.py, decision.py, preprocess.py, analysis/failure_decomposition.py, benchmark_tests.py, window_thresholds.py, experiments/feature_groups.py, pairwise_transfer.py header, paper/build_ledger.py). NO paper PDF and NO result files in deposit (README: 'saved scores ... will be deposited'; GitHub repo not reachable from this session).
a: PARTLY DONE. E2 'failure decomposition' asks 'Is the failure network-driven or caused by novel attacks?': per run, AUROC of target-benign vs seen-family target attacks and vs novel-family target attacks; at threshold = 99th pct of source-validation benign scores, reports realised target benign FPR ('tgt_benignFPR_at_srcFPR1') and target attack TPR ('tgt_TPR_at_srcFPR1') vs source TPR. Pre-declared H-F1: seen-family AUROC < 0.75 on >=2/4 targets. They do NOT score source-benign vs target-attack or target-benign vs source-attack cross pairs, and do not swap benign/attack across domains. Numbers UNVERIFIED (not in deposit).
b: PARTLY DONE. E7: XGBoost (n_estimators=100, depth 6) retrained under LODO without one group: TTL {MIN_TTL,MAX_TTL,DNS_TTL_ANSWER}; TCP window {TCP_WIN_MAX_IN/OUT}; timing {durations + 8 IAT}; 'artifacts' = TTL+TCP window+L4_SRC/DST_PORT,DNS_QUERY_ID,ICMP_TYPE,ICMP_IPV4_TYPE,FTP_COMMAND_RET_CODE. Reports target AUROC and target-benign FPR at source-calibrated 1% FPR threshold; labelled 'association only'. E4 identifier-free features (drop ports, DNS_QUERY_ID, ICMP types, FTP ret code) rerun for 6 methods. E6 pairwise: Spearman of transfer loss vs benign-source-vs-benign-target divergence (mean PSI, normalised Wasserstein, standardised mean diff) - 'audit gate'. NO transplant/counterfactual swaps of a group's benign distribution, no sizes/DNS-only groups. Numbers UNVERIFIED.
c: YES, extensively. S1 (unlabelled 1,500-flow target buffer at natural prior): CORAL, DANN, IW-DANN, DANN-R, AdaBN, TENT, DomNorm (per-testbed z-score; target z-scored with buffer). S2 (500-flow target 'reference window' = 475 benign + 25 attack, 5% contamination): BRN = benign-referenced normalisation (each source z-scored by its own benign training flows, target by window stats, after log1p; clip +-5, sd floor 0.1) + MLP or XGBoost; IF-win; KNN-win. Thresholds: 'em' (temperature scaling + Saerens EM prior on buffer, max expected Macro-F1), win_mad (median+3*1.4826*MAD of window scores), win_fpr (99th pct of window scores). Follow-ups: window size {50..2000}, contamination {0..30%}, temporal window before monitored period (E5-T), window poisoning + trimming defence, BRN-vs-DomNorm hypothesis H-B4, HYB (ECDF-normalised BRN+KNN-win average, H-E8). Results UNVERIFIED (no numbers in deposit).
d: YES. IF-win (isolation forest fitted on target window only, no source training) and KNN-win (mean distance to k nearest window flows in window-z-scored space) are pure target-benign novelty scorers; quantile (win_fpr) and MAD thresholds on window scores; HYB combines BRN with KNN-win via window ECDF. Conformal framing not used explicitly but win_fpr is a split-quantile rule.
e: LODO on NF-v3 (and NF-v2), 4 targets x 10 seeds, 100k-flow target eval stream at natural prior, 100k flows per source (80/20). Primary metric AUROC; secondary Macro-F1, realised FPR/TPR, TPR@1%/0.1% FPR, PR-AUC, per-family recall. Tuning: leave-one-source-out, 12 configs, select by mean AUROC. 49 NF-v3 features (no IPs, no timestamps). Exact numbers: UNVERIFIED (paper and results not public in deposit).
f: 18: S0 ERM, ERM-CB, XGB, RF, IRM, V-REx, GroupDRO; S1 CORAL, DANN, IW-DANN, DANN-R, AdaBN, TENT, DomNorm; S2 BRN, BRN-XGB, IF-win, KNN-win; S3 (label-budget study) XGB-T, XGB-ST (k in 10..1000). Plus diagnostics BBSE, true-prior em, oracle threshold, HYB.
notes: Most threatening work: covers our RQ1 grid, a benign-referenced normalisation remedy (BRN, with DomNorm mixture control), target-benign window novelty detectors and label-free window thresholds, a benign-FPR/attack-TPR split, feature-group ablation of TTL/TCP-window/timing/ports, and a benign-divergence audit. Deposit published 2026-11-12; paper venue TBA.

work: P04 Valencia Velez 2026, 'Auditing the NetFlow versions of IoT and enterprise intrusion detection benchmarks: data quality, shortcuts and cross-dataset evaluation' (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23291191 -> record 23291192; submitted to Computer Networks)
source_opened: Full code+results archive: README, scripts/44_cross_dataset.py docstring, nfv3_config.py feature sets, data/eval/cross_report.txt, cross_inspection.txt, exploration/{dns_ttl_anomaly,src_port_signal,n5_threshold_check}.txt. Paper PDF not in deposit.
a: No explicit benign-vs-attack-shift decomposition. Diagnostics only: CORE confusion matrices into NF-BoT-IoT (e.g. ToN-v3->BoT-v3 xgb: target Benign 94.6% predicted Benign, DoS/DDoS 99.7% predicted Benign - i.e. failure is missed attacks there); n5_threshold_check reports attack recall at thresholds set at target-benign p95/p90 (uses target labels; diagnostic) for ->BoT-IoT pairs.
b: Shortcut probes (depth-1..3 trees per class vs benign, within dataset); src_port_signal (single-port RF macro-F1 class vs benign); dns_ttl_anomaly (DNS_TTL_ANSWER values ~4.29e9 in 320 BoT-IoT-v3 Reconnaissance rows); cross-dataset feature-set conditions: G0 (all but L4_SRC_PORT), G-NP (no dst port), G-NI (no ports, TTL, TCP window, DNS), G-NIS0 (also no L7_PROTO/ICMP types); SHAP + RF permutation importance. Result (BIN, 24 direction x model): G-NP worse in 13, G-NI worse in 16 vs G0 -> removal mostly hurts. No transplant tests; no attribution to benign shift.
c: None (source-only training; no target normalisation or adaptation).
e: Pairwise (not LODO), 3 datasets (no UNSW), binary macro-F1 at default argmax, XGBoost & RF, 5 seeds, target = all rows. NF-v3 G0 BIN target macro-F1 (xgb/rf): BoT->CIC 0.687/0.613; BoT->ToN 0.397/0.519; CIC->BoT 0.129/0.087; CIC->ToN 0.692/0.444; ToN->BoT 0.492/0.329; ToN->CIC 0.420/0.430. In-domain G0: BoT 0.827/0.861, CIC 0.945/0.832, ToN 0.843/0.862.
f: XGBoost, Random Forest; conditions G0, R0 (random split), G-NC (no label conflicts), G-NP, G-NI, G-NIS0; tasks BIN, CORE (Benign/DoS/DDoS), EXT; replication of Layeghy & Portmann 2023; Flood et al. 2024 heuristics.
